resale_co.name: Certificate of Occupancy / Certificate of Approval (Change of Occupancy housing inspection)
resale_co.issued_by: City of Bordentown Department of Housing, Zoning & Code Enforcement (Housing Inspector)
resale_co.lead_time: Apply at least 14 days but not more than 30 days before the change in occupancy; the FAQ says allow at least 2 weeks to get the first inspection appointment.
requirements: Smoke alarms on every level and outside each sleeping area; replace alarms older than 10 years; battery units must be 10-year sealed
Carbon monoxide alarm near the bedrooms if there are fuel-burning appliances or an attached garage
Fire extinguisher at least 2A:10B:C (see fire certificate details)
Electrical: 100-amp minimum service, outlets grounded with cover plates, GFI outlets in bathrooms, panel door and no open slots
Plumbing: no leaks, J-bend sink drains, water heater relief pipe to 6 inches above floor, hot water 120 to 140 degrees F, backflow devices, water meter installed
Sump pump works and opening is covered
Floors, walls and ceilings sound and free of holes, trip hazards and peeling paint
Kitchen: stove, oven and broiler work; anti-tip bracket on range; cabinets intact
Windows open, stay open, lock and have intact screens; doors latch, exterior and bathroom doors lock
Graspable handrails on 3 or more steps; porch and deck railings with openings no more than 4 inches
Roofing certification if there are signs of active leaks; Level II chimney certification for wood stoves or wood fireplaces
Exterior, gutters, fences, sidewalks, driveways and patios in safe repair; trip hazards on adjacent sidewalks must be fixed
Visible structural defects fixed; yard mowed and cleared of junk and debris
Work done without permits must be permitted and inspected before the CO is issued
House number visible from the street (front and back if on an alley)
resale_co.how_to_apply: Fill out the Change of Occupancy Application (Certificate of Occupancy Application in the city's Application & Forms folder), pay the fee, and send it to the Department of Housing, Zoning & Code Enforcement, 101 E. Park Street, Bordentown, NJ 08505 (planning@cityofbordentown.com). The next available inspection is scheduled once the form is filed and paid. Vacant homes can use a lock box; otherwise someone 18 or older must let the inspector in.

evidence.quote: A Certificate of Occupancy is required in Bordentown City when selling or purchasing a property, when there is a change in occupancy, or when a property is to be rented out.
The housing inspection conducted by Bordentown City is the basis for the issuance of a ... of Approval as required by Chapter 216, City of Bordentown code.
Request for inspection must be made at least (14) days, but not more than (30) days, prior to the change in occupancy of the dwelling.
Department of Housing, Zoning & Code Enforcement 101 E. Park Street Bordentown NJ 08505 planning@cityofbordentown.com
Please allow at least 2 weeks for scheduling your initial inspection appointment.
The City of Bordentown Housing Department no longer issues Temporary ... of Occupancy.

resale_co.notes: The city's live website (cityofbordentown.com) shows a browser challenge page, so the documents were fetched from the city's own document host (files-backend.assets.thrillshare.com), whose links are listed in the city's Application & Forms folder. The current Change of Occupancy Application (file dated May 2026) raised the resale fee to $125 and re-inspection to $50; an older rev 9-2022 form showed Housing Resale $75.00 and Reinspection $20.00 and gave phone (609) 298-0604 ext 4. Buyers purchasing 'As-Is' can request a 'No Occupancy' letter for closing (application and fee still required, plus the signed as-is contract and a signed buyer letter); no temporary COs. Staff directory lists Charles Latini for Housing/Code Enforcement without a phone or email, so the office email from the form is given. Rental units also need annual landlord registration and a lead-safe certificate at tenant turnover ($25 city filing fee).

requirements: Smoke alarms must be replaced after 10 years; battery alarms must be 10-year sealed (ANSI/UL 217); hardwired alarms from original construction stay hardwired
Required alarm type depends on the year the house was built (for example 1984-1990 electric interconnected on all levels; 1992 to present electric interconnected in all bedrooms with battery backup)
Carbon monoxide alarm near the bedrooms if fuel-burning appliances or an attached garage (UL 2034)
Fire extinguisher at least 2A:10B:C, no more than 10 lb, within 10 feet of the kitchen, top no higher than 5 feet, on the maker's bracket, near an exit path
Extinguisher must be tagged by a Division of Fire Safety certified contractor within 12 months or have a recent purchase receipt; leave the owner's manual; do not remove the tamper seal

authorities.name: City of Bordentown Department of Housing, Zoning & Code Enforcement (smoke, CO and extinguisher checked in the city housing inspection)
authorities.lead_time: Apply 14 to 30 days before the change in occupancy

fees.label: Combined resale housing inspection including smoke/CO/extinguisher (paid once)

authorities.how_to_apply: Part of the city Change of Occupancy Application; no separate smoke certificate application was found.

evidence.quote: Required in all buildings that contain fuel burning appliances or that have an attached garage.
SMOKE DETECTOR REQUIREMENT FOR CHANGE OF OCCUPANCY
The extinguisher shall be serviced and tagged by a certified Division of Fire Safety contractor within the past 12 months or must have a receipt for a recently purchased extinguisher.

fire_cert.notes: The state fire code enforcing agency for Bordentown City is Bordentown Township Fire District #1 (Mission Fire Company Fire Prevention Bureau, Fire Marshal Mark Mezger, (609) 298-5375, mmezger@missionfire.org), per the DCA LEA registry and directory. But the DCA directory lists 'Bordentown City Inspection Dept' (324 Farnsworth Av, (609) 298-9046, an older city address) under smoke detector compliance, and the city's own change-of-occupancy packet checks smoke alarms, CO alarms and the extinguisher as part of the city housing inspection. Under N.J.A.C. 5:70-2.3(a)1 a municipal resale inspection replaces the separate state certificate, so no separate fire district smoke certificate fee was found. The city's extinguisher sheet (December 2024) still requires an extinguisher even though P.L.2025, c.19 (February 3, 2025) removed it from the state rule.

other_items.label: Open permits
other_items.detail: Work done without required permits must be permitted and inspected before the CO is issued. Open permits and violations can be checked with an OPRA request to the Municipal Clerk.

other_items.label: As-is purchase
other_items.detail: Buyer can request a 'No Occupancy' letter for closing; the application and fee, signed as-is contract and a signed buyer letter are required, and the buyer signs the letter at the Housing Inspection Office.

other_items.label: Chimney certification
other_items.detail: Level II chimney inspection by a qualified chimney sweep for solid fuel stoves or wood burning fireplaces.

other_items.label: Roofing certification
other_items.detail: Required from a licensed roofer if there is interior evidence of active leaks.
